output.name: Nethára — "the Mussel Basket"
output.myth: When Aun cut the string and the sky drifted off, the shore birds were left with nothing to wind. Hesk saw it and kept count, as she does. Kessal, whose bill is a red knife, was already at work. Every low tide she went down to the rock and prised mussels off one by one. The good ones went in the old women's baskets, the bad ones into her own gullet, and she never said a word. The fishers ate and forgot her. Ennu the Kite-Wright noticed. He said nothing either, which is how Ennu says most things. He cut a small kite from the spare sail and flew it over the rock, near enough for Kessal to see the mark on her own bill. Up at the pole the Drop Spindle turned, and Hesk tied one knot for her in the count. Hirun, the bent-footed gull, flew that count up from the rock, complaining of the weather all the way. Kessal was pleased. She did not tell anyone. Fly a kite for her when your hands are sore from work nobody thanked you for.
output.finding: Start at the Drop Spindle, which never sets, and go a little under one hand-span (about 16°) due south to find the Knife-Beak.
